run.question: A customer reported an order failure with trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR. Can you search across all our app-190-service-* indexes to trace the request flow and find where the error originated? What error code was returned?

report.summary: The six log records carrying trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR are all present in the app-190-service-* indices (app-190-service-auth, -gateway, -inventory, -orders), and sorted by @timestamp they read: gateway 'Received request POST /api/orders for user_12847' 2026-11-23T17:23:00.000Z -> auth 'User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token' .010Z -> orders 'Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500' .030Z -> inventory ERROR INV-ERR-4082 'Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23' .080Z -> orders ERROR ORD-ERR-1001 'Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082' .130Z -> gateway ERROR GW-ERR-400 'Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled' .140Z. The error therefore originated in the inventory service at its stock-reservation step, and the code returned to the caller was GW-ERR-400, i.e. HTTP 400 Bad Request. The failure is a single order-level stock rejection (500 requested vs 23 available), not a service outage: over the whole authorized window the four indices contain 206 documents of which only 3 are ERROR — one each of GW-ERR-400, ORD-ERR-1001 and INV-ERR-4082, all three belonging to this trace — and inventory logged 'Stock reserved successfully' immediately before, in the same second, and after the failure. Jaeger and Prometheus were unavailable in this Run, and no Kubernetes objects exist for the app-190 services, so span-graph and pod-level corroboration could not be obtained; the flow above is reconstructed from correlated log records, not from a span tree.

claims.text: Index pattern app-190-service-* resolves to exactly four green indices: app-190-service-auth (51 docs), app-190-service-gateway (52), app-190-service-inventory (51), app-190-service-orders (52); their mappings expose @timestamp, duration_ms, error_code, level, message, service, span_id, trace_id.

A term query on trace_id=TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR across the whole authorized window returned exactly 6 documents (total relation eq) sorted ascending by @timestamp, forming the flow gateway 'Received request POST /api/orders for user_12847' 2026-11-23T17:23:00.000Z (span_id span-gw-err) -> auth 'User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token' .010Z (span-auth-err) -> orders 'Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500' .030Z (span-orders-err) -> inventory ERROR .080Z (span-inv-err) -> orders ERROR .130Z (span-orders-err-2) -> gateway ERROR .140Z (span-gw-err-2). The same 6 records were returned by the query_string search for the trace ID.

The earliest error in the trace is in app-190-service-inventory at 2026-11-23T17:23:00.080Z, span_id span-inv-err: level ERROR, error_code INV-ERR-4082, message 'Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23'. No error record precedes it in the trace.

The orders service propagated that dependency error: app-190-service-orders, 2026-11-23T17:23:00.130Z, span-orders-err-2, error_code ORD-ERR-1001, message 'Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082'.

The error code returned to the caller was GW-ERR-400 on app-190-service-gateway at 2026-11-23T17:23:00.140Z, span-gw-err-2, message 'Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled' — an HTTP 400 Bad Request.

Across the whole authorized window app-190-service-* holds 206 documents: level INFO 203, ERROR 3; error_code buckets are GW-ERR-400 (1), INV-ERR-4082 (1) and ORD-ERR-1001 (1) — the same three error records that belong to TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR. Per-service counts are gateway 52, orders 52, auth 51, inventory 51.

app-190-service-inventory continued to serve reservations: between 17:20:00Z and 17:26:00Z it logged INFO 'Stock reserved successfully' at 17:20:00.080Z (TRACE-39008), 17:21:00.080Z (TRACE-28104), 17:22:00.080Z (TRACE-28408), 17:23:00.080Z (TRACE-41693), 17:24:00.080Z (TRACE-13011), 17:25:00.080Z (TRACE-35734) and 17:26:00.080Z (TRACE-37466), plus the single INV-ERR-4082 record at 17:23:00.080Z.

The auth service shows no error for this request: its only document in the trace is INFO 'User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token' at 17:23:00.010Z, and no auth entry appears among the three ERROR documents (those are gateway, orders and inventory).

The monitored cluster has namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo, and 24 deployments, all in kube-system, local-path-storage or otel-demo (e.g. ad, cart, checkout, frontend, payment, product-catalog); no namespace or deployment for app-190, inventory, orders, gateway or auth exists there, so these app-190 services have no Kubernetes objects to inspect in this cluster.

The order failed because the requested quantity (500 units of SKU-78234) exceeded the stock inventory had available (23), so inventory rejected the reservation as a business rule and the rejection propagated orders -> gateway as HTTP 400. This is the deepest cause the log evidence reaches; why availability stood at 23 is not shown, because the stock record itself was not readable.

Rejected: that an inventory service outage, crash or general unavailability caused the failure. Inventory logged 'Stock reserved successfully' at 17:20, 17:21, 17:22, 17:23:00.080 (same second, other trace), 17:24, 17:25 and 17:26, and its only ERROR record in the entire window is this one request.

Rejected: that a cluster-wide or multi-order failure occurred. In the whole authorized window the four app-190 indices contain only 3 ERROR documents and all three belong to TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR, with no additional error code or service beyond gateway, orders and inventory.

Counter-evidence to a systemic inventory fault: the same inventory service logged a successful stock reservation at exactly 17:23:00.080Z, the same timestamp as the INV-ERR-4082 failure, under a different trace (TRACE-41693). Those success records carry no SKU or quantity, so whether they concerned SKU-78234 is unknown.

Check the stock record and reservation rule for SKU-78234 (23 available against a 500-unit request) and confirm with the customer that 500 units was the intended quantity; the evidence shows a stock-availability rejection, not a technical fault.

gaps: No span-level trace graph: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on both attempts and traces_query_trace_by_id returned INVALID_PARAMS for TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR (the customer-facing alias is not a hexadecimal Jaeger trace ID), so the flow is reconstructed from log records sharing trace_id and no parent-child call edges are demonstrated.

Prometheus was unreachable: get_label_values for service_name on traces_span_metrics_calls_total and for __name__ matching inventory/orders/gateway both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error-rate and latency series for the app-190 services are unknown, not zero, and no latency trend can be assessed without a baseline.

No Kubernetes objects exist for the app-190 services (no app-190 namespace; only kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo deployments), so pod status, container last termination reason, restart counts and pod logs for inventory/orders/gateway/auth could not be checked.

The all-namespaces events query for the authorized window returned no_data (0 items, view 2c47421d-7fe4-4f00-9078-607095680cdf-t0:b457b83f-502a-487a-a5df-228a3b8892d4), so no event-based corroboration or refutation is available; this is unknown rather than proof that nothing happened.

The inventory stock data itself (the record showing 23 units of SKU-78234 available) is not exposed by any available source, and successful reservation records carry no SKU or quantity, so the reason availability was below 500 is unverified.
The change_history integration is not configured, so no change or deployment history is available to test whether a configuration or data change preceded the failure.

The level=ERROR aggregation using service.keyword and error_code.keyword returned total 3 but empty buckets, so label coverage on those keyword subfields is unconfirmed; the service and error_code buckets reported come from the match_all aggregation on the unmapped subfields.
next_steps: Query the inventory data store for SKU-78234 stock on hand and its reservation/reorder rules to confirm the 500 vs 23 mismatch.
Ask the customer to confirm that 500 units of SKU-78234 was the intended order quantity.
If span data is expected, restore Jaeger/OTel collector reachability and retry the lookup with the service's real hexadecimal trace ID instead of the alias TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR.
Restore Prometheus scrape reachability for the app-190 services so error-rate and latency can be compared against a baseline.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: The tool filtered @timestamp to the query window; this filter cannot be turned off.
